origin: A short mark above a long line. The long stroke is a baseline; whatever sits over it is above.
note: 上手 じょうず is jukujikun — the compound carries its own reading. Don't read it as じょう plus ず.

origin: The same drawing flipped: a mark below the line.
note: 下手 へた is irregular the same way: 下 is した or か everywhere else, and へ only there.

origin: A drawing of a hand — the crossing strokes are the fingers, the hooked downstroke the arm. On the left of other kanji it shrinks to 扌.
note: The same 手 sits in 上手 and 下手, read ず and た — neither is a normal reading of it.

origin: 女 woman + 子 child: a mother holding her child — what you love.
note: Regular: 好 is す and the き is okurigana.

origin: 女 woman + 兼 (a hand holding two stalks), which gives the sound けん. 女 is the meaning side, as in a number of old characters for feelings.
note: Regular: 嫌 is きら and the い is okurigana.

origin: A person seen from the side: two legs, leaning forward as they walk. On the left of other kanji it stands up straight as 亻.
note: Counting people switches to にん — ひとり, ふたり, さんにん.

origin: Three peaks: a mountain range drawn as simply as possible.
note: 富士山 is ふじさん — the on-reading さん, not やま.

origin: Water flowing between two banks — three lines running downhill.
A stream down the middle with splashes on either side. On the left of other kanji it becomes three drops, 氵: 海, 港, 涼.
note: 水曜日 すいようび uses すい, the on-reading.

origin: A crescent moon. Inside other kanji the same shape is often a squeezed 肉, flesh, and has nothing to do with the moon — as in 祭.
note: げつ in 月曜日, がつ in the month names — 四月 しがつ.

origin: 穴 a hole or cave + 工, which gives the sound くう: the hollow overhead — empty, and the sky.
The top line is the sky, the frame a cloud hanging from it, and the four dots drops falling. On top of other kanji it marks weather: 雪, 雲, 曇.
note: Same reading as 飴 あめ, sweets — different kanji, different pitch.

origin: 艹 plants + 化 change, which also gives the sound か: the part of a plant that changes — the flower.
note: Same reading as 鼻 はな, nose.

origin: A cart seen from above: the box in the middle, the axle running through it, the two wheels at top and bottom.
note: しゃ in compounds — 電車 でんしゃ, 自転車 じてんしゃ.

origin: 木 a tree with a stroke across its foot marking the root — the origin of something. Book came later.
note: Here the everyday reading is the on-reading ほん, as in 日本 にほん.

origin: A fish standing on its tail: head on top, scaled body in the middle, and the four dots are the tail fin — not fire, though they look the same.
Once a drawing of a dog. Today it is 大 with a dot — read the dot as the ear.
An open mouth. It also means any opening: 入口 いりぐち, the way in.
note: 入口 いりぐち and 出口 でぐち voice it to ぐち.

origin: A drawing of an ear, the lobe at the bottom.
The box on top is the knee, the rest is the leg and the foot below it.
A line straight through the middle of a box — originally a banner pole planted in the centre of a camp.
note: ちゅう in compounds — 中国 ちゅうごく, China.

origin: 夕 evening + 卜, the crack read in a divination bone. The traditional explanation: divining in the evening was outside the proper time — so, outside.
note: がい in compounds — 外国 がいこく, a foreign country.

origin: The top was a foot (止) and the 月 a boat (舟): moving forward in a boat — the front, ahead. 刂, a blade, was added later. None of the parts still looks like what it was.
note: ぜん in compounds — 午前 ごぜん, the morning half of the clock.

origin: The top is a hand (ナ) and 口 a mouth: the hand that feeds you — the right one.
The same hand (ナ) with 工, a carpenter's square: the hand that holds the work steady while the right one does it.
note: 左 and 右 differ in stroke order, not just shape: 左 starts with the horizontal, 右 with the sweep.

origin: 門 a gate + 日 the sun: light showing through the gap between the doors — a gap, the space between. The old form had the moon (閒) instead.
note: かん in compounds — 時間 じかん, time. Alone it is あいだ.

origin: 阝 + 粦, which gives the sound りん. In the older form 鄰 the 阝 sat on the right, where it means a village: the people next door.
note: となり is the next one in a row; for merely beside something you want よこ.

origin: 彳 a road + 幺 a thread + 夂 a dragging foot: walking with your feet tied, so you fall behind — behind, after.
note: Three readings worth knowing: うしろ behind, ご in 午後 ごご the afternoon, あと in 後で あとで, later.

origin: 辶 the road + 斤 an axe, which only gives the sound きん: not far along the road. 辶 carries the distance and speed words: 近, 遠, 速, 遅.
note: 近い ちかい is the adjective, 近く the place. きん in compounds — 最近 さいきん, lately.

origin: 罒 a net over 貝 a cowrie shell — shells were money. Netting valuables: to buy. 貝 runs through most of the money kanji.
note: Dictionary form 買う かう; 買い物 かいもの is shopping. The lid on top is 罒, a net — not 四.

origin: A flag (the 方 side and the top) flying over people: a band marching under a banner. It meant a troop first, then a journey.
note: たび on its own is a journey; りょ in 旅行.

origin: A crossroads seen from above, split into two halves (彳 and 亍): where you go.
note: こう in compounds — 旅行 りょこう, 銀行 ぎんこう, 航空便 こうくうびん.

origin: Made in Japan, not China: 亻 a person + 動 move — a person in motion, working. 動 is itself 重 heavy + 力 strength.
note: 人 on the left, 動 (move) on the right — a person moving.

origin: 力 strength + 免, which gives the sound べん: straining your strength — effort.
note: Turns up almost only in 勉強.

origin: 弓 a bow + 厶 + 虫 an insect. It first named a kind of insect, with 弘 giving the sound; strong is a borrowed meaning. A drawn bow is a fair hook to remember it by.
note: つよい is strong; きょう in 勉強 — studying as forcing yourself.

origin: One stroke for one.
note: ひと in 一つ ひとつ and 一人 ひとり.

origin: Two strokes for two, the bottom one longer.
note: ふた in 二つ ふたつ and 二人 ふたり.

origin: Three strokes for three, the middle one shortest.
note: み in 三つ みっつ and 三日 みっか.

origin: Originally four lines, like 一 二 三. This shape — breath coming out of a mouth — was borrowed because four lines were too easy to misread.
note: Three readings and the counter picks: 四時 よじ, 四日 よっか, 四月 しがつ.

origin: Originally an X between two lines, a sign for five. The X has been squared off into the middle strokes.
note: いつ in 五つ いつつ and 五日 いつか.

origin: Most likely a little hut — a roof on two posts — borrowed for its sound to write six.
note: む in 六つ むっつ and 六日 むいか.

origin: Originally a cross meaning to cut (it is still inside 切). Borrowed for seven, with the tail bent so it couldn't be mistaken for 十.
note: しち in 七時 しちじ; 七日 is なのか, which follows neither.

origin: Two strokes parting from each other — to divide (分 still has it on top). Borrowed for eight. It widens toward the bottom, which is why eight counts as lucky.
note: や in 八つ やっつ; 八日 is ようか, an outlier.

origin: Thought to be a bent arm, borrowed for nine.
note: く in 九時 くじ and 九月 くがつ; ここの in 九日 ここのか.

origin: Originally a vertical line with a knot in the middle — a knot on a counting cord. The knot grew into the crossbar.
note: とお in 十 とお and 十日 とおか.

origin: The sun: a circle with a dot in the middle, squared off, the dot stretched into a line.
note: 今日 きょう is jukujikun — the compound has its own reading. Elsewhere: にち in 日曜日, か in 三日 みっか, び closing 曜日.

origin: 日 sun + 翟, a pheasant with bright feathers (羽 over 隹), which gives the sound よう: the shining bodies of the sky — sun, moon and five planets, the seven the weekdays are named after.
note: Appears only in the seven weekday names.

origin: 日 sun + 寺 a temple, which gives the sound じ. The sun's movement measures time — and temple bells rang the hours, a handy hook.
note: じ is the o'clock counter — 四時 よじ. じかん is a span of hours.

origin: 辶 movement + 周 all the way round, which also gives the sound しゅう: one full round — a week.
note: Always しゅう: 先週, 来週, 週末, 一週間.

origin: Originally 禾 ripe grain over 人 a person: someone carrying the harvest home. One harvest, one year.
note: とし in 今年 ことし and 毎年 まいとし; ねん in 一年 いちねん.

origin: A lid closing over something: what is held right here — now. The parts have worn too smooth to read; learn it as a shape.
note: こん in 今週 こんしゅう and 今晩 こんばん; 今日 and 今朝 go their own way.

origin: 亻 a person + 可, which gives the sound か. It first drew someone with a load on their shoulder; once it was borrowed for 'what', 艹 was added to make 荷, load, for the old meaning.
note: なん before a counter — 何人, 何時, 何枚. なに on its own.

origin: A foot (the top, from 止) placed in front of a person (儿): going ahead — first, earlier.
note: Ahead in space, earlier in time: 先週 last week, 先月 last month.

origin: 气, rising vapour, over what used to be 米 rice (old form 氣): steam from cooking rice — breath, air, spirit. The Japanese form swaps the rice for a simple ×.
note: 元気 げんき well, 気温 きおん air temperature, 病気 びょうき illness.

origin: Old form 學: two hands passing on knowledge (爻) to a child (子) under a roof. The Japanese form squeezes the top into three dots and a lid.
note: 学生 がくせい a student, 大学 だいがく a university.

origin: 宀 a roof + 豕 a pig: pigs kept under the same roof as the family — a home.
note: うち is the same kanji and means home as in my household; か in 作家 さっか, a writer.

origin: Stands in for the older 臺, a raised platform. Its own parts, 厶 and 口, came from a different word, so read the whole as a stand or base.
note: The counter for machines and vehicles — 3台 さんだい. Regular from 1 to 10.

origin: 口 over 儿 legs: a person who is all mouth — by the traditional reading, the one who speaks for the family: the older brother.
note: にい in お兄さん おにいさん, someone else's older brother; けい in 兄弟 きょうだい.

origin: 女 woman + a right side that looks like 市, market, but only gives the sound し: the older sister.
note: ねえ in お姉さん おねえさん.

origin: A cord wound around a stake, turn after turn — order, sequence. The one who comes next: the younger brother.
note: だい in 兄弟 きょうだい, brothers and sisters.

origin: 女 woman + 未 not yet, which gives the sound まい: a sister not yet grown — the younger one.
note: まい in 姉妹 しまい, sisters.

origin: 目 an eye on 儿 legs: a person who is all eye — seeing.
note: An eye 目 on legs. けん in 意見 いけん, an opinion.

origin: 小 small with a slash taking a bit more away: smaller still — few, a little.
note: すこ in 少し すこし, a little — the adverb, where 少ない is the adjective.

origin: Two 夕 stacked — originally two pieces of meat piled up: more than one, many.
note: た in 多分 たぶん, probably.

origin: A mouth with something held inside it, savoured: sweet.
A drawing of a needle once used to tattoo criminals: sharp pain. Spicy is the same sting on the tongue, and 辛い read つらい is hardship.
note: The same 辛い read つらい means painful, hard to bear — context picks.

origin: A person straining under a tied sack (the 東-like middle): heavy. 重 plus 力 strength makes 動, to move.
note: じゅう in 体重 たいじゅう, body weight.

origin: 車 a cart + 圣 (from 巠), which gives the sound けい: a light cart — light in weight. The old form is 輕.
note: 車 on the left — けい in 軽自動車 けいじどうしゃ, a small kei car.

origin: 辶 the road + 袁 a long trailing robe, which gives the sound えん: a long way down the road — far.
note: えん in 遠足 えんそく, a school outing.

origin: 日 the sun over 十 — traditionally read as the sun just breaking over the horizon: early morning, early.
note: Early in time. Fast in speed is 速い — the same はやい, a different kanji.

origin: 辶 the road + 束 a bundle, which gives the sound そく: moving along the road quickly — fast.
note: Speed, not time. そく in 速達 そくたつ, special delivery.

origin: 辶 the road + an old character for a rhinoceros (犀, still visible in the old form 遲) for the sound; the Japanese form trims it to 尸 over 羊. A rhino lumbering down the road: late, slow.
note: One kanji for both: late is the opposite of 早い, slow of 速い. ち in 遅刻 ちこく, being late.

origin: ⺮ bamboo + 間, which gives the sound かん: letters were written on strips of bamboo — a short note, so brief, simple.
note: ⺮, bamboo, on top. Turns up almost only in 簡単.

origin: Simplified from 單, a forked club used in hunting — one tool, a single thing. The Japanese form turns its two loops into three dots.
note: たん in 単語 たんご, a word of vocabulary.

origin: Originally 艸 plants and 屯, a shoot pushing up through the soil, over 日 the sun — the season things sprout. The top has worn into 三 over 人.
note: 春休み はるやすみ, the spring holidays.

origin: A whole person drawn from head (the 自 part, from 頁) to foot (夂). Summer is a borrowed meaning — the drawing doesn't show it.
note: 夏休み なつやすみ, the summer holidays.

origin: 禾 grain + 火 fire: the harvest season, when the stubble was burned off the fields.
The top was a cord knotted at both ends — the end, as in 終; the two dots underneath are ice (冫). The end of the year, the icy one.
禾 grain over 子 a child: the young crop growing through its season — a season.
note: 四季 しき, the four seasons.

origin: ⺮ bamboo + 即, which gives the sound せつ: the joint in a bamboo stalk. A stalk is divided by its joints the way a year is by its seasons.
note: ⺮, bamboo, on top — a joint in the stalk, hence a division of the year.

origin: 氵 water + 巷 an alley between houses, which gives the sound こう: a street of water, where the boats come in — a harbour.
note: An airport is a sky harbour: 空 + 港. みなと on its own is a harbour.

origin: 氵 water + 毎 every, which gives the sound (かい): the water that is everywhere — the sea.
note: かい in 海外 かいがい, overseas.

origin: 糸 thread + 工, which gives the sound こう: dyed thread — crimson, the red of dyed silk.
note: 紅葉 もみじ is jukujikun — the compound carries its own reading. Read こうよう it is the leaves turning. こう in 紅茶 こうちゃ, black tea.

origin: 艹 plants over 世 on 木 a tree — the 世 was the leaves on the branches: leaves.
note: Alone it is は, a leaf; よう in 紅葉 read こうよう. Inside もみじ it has no reading of its own.

origin: Simplified from 壽, which put 老 old age over a long winding furrow: a long life. The Japanese form keeps only an outline of it.
note: 寿司 is ateji — kanji chosen for their sound, す + し, and for luck: 寿 means long life.

origin: A hand (the hooked outer stroke) over 口 a mouth: someone giving orders — in charge, administering.
note: し is a real reading here, as in 司会 しかい, an MC.

origin: 大, a person with arms spread, with a line above the head: what is above a person — the sky, heaven.
note: The same てん in 天ぷら てんぷら.

origin: 火 fire + 尭 (from 堯, earth heaped high), which gives the sound: a fire piled high — burning, grilling. The old form is 燒.
note: 焼き鳥 やきとり, grilled chicken on skewers.

origin: 朿 a thorn + 刂 a blade: something sharp that goes in — to pierce, to stab.
note: し in 名刺 めいし, a business card.

origin: A drawing of a person with a swollen belly — pregnant, the body itself. Flesh, and oneself.
note: み is the flesh — 刺身 is pierced flesh. しん in 身長 しんちょう, height.

origin: 月 (here 肉, meat) + 又 a hand + 示 an altar: a hand placing meat on the altar. A festival began as an offering to the gods.
note: さい in 文化祭 ぶんかさい, a school festival.

origin: 言 words + 式 a set form, which gives the sound し: putting set questions to someone — to test, to try.
note: ため in 試します ためします, to try something out.

origin: 馬 a horse + a right side that gives the sound けん: originally examining a horse — to test, to check. The old form is 驗.
note: 馬, horse, on the left. けん in 経験 けいけん, experience.

origin: 雨 weather over a hand holding a broom (from 彗, cut down to ヨ): what falls and has to be swept away — snow.
note: 雨 on top — the weather kanji wear the rain radical: 雪, 雲, 電.

origin: 日 the sun over 雲 a cloud: the sun hidden behind cloud — cloudy.
note: 日 over 雲 — the sun behind a cloud.

origin: 日 sun + 爰, which gives the sound だん: the sun's warmth — warm air, warm weather.
note: Warm air and weather. 温かい, the same reading, is warm to the touch — food, a bath.

origin: 氵 water + 京 a capital, which gives the sound りょう: cool water — cool, refreshing.
note: Cool air only — a cool drink is 冷たい.
